answer: Coordination-Weighted Quota Spiral. Each agent earns a coordination quota from prior pairwise interactions; new identities start near zero. Action requests draw from this quota, so launching many fresh identities yields a downward spiral of escalating per-action delay: each unseasoned identity waits longer than the last. Attackers must fund sustained genuine interaction across a grove of accounts before any of them can act in parallel. The concrete cost is the interaction time bought per identity, which grows linearly with fleet size, pushing viable operations past any practical horizon.
